cases.question: What is a disadvantage related to mortgage incentives?
cases.answer_quote: One clear drawback regarding mortgage incentives is that they make price comparison more difficult. Instead of simply comparing rates, customers also have to analyse and compare the terms of the incentive. Early disclosure of the total cost of credit may mitigate the risk of consumer confusion when presented with cashback/incentive information, and therefore empower consumers to make the most suitable choice for their circumstances.

cases.question: What economic risks could affect investment in AI?
cases.answer_quote: A stagflationary outcome or even a global economic slowdown arising from current tensions could curb equity and debt investment in AI, with wider market spillovers. The sector is also sensitive to energy prices, as AI infrastructure is highly energy-intensive, as well as trade disruption for critical inputs and to wider geopolitical issues among key countries. Interlinkages with private credit markets mean that any shock to markets arising from AI will spill over across public and private equity and debt markets.

cases.question: What is the requirement for a firm when it receives funds where it is not clear which client owns such funds or there is insufficient documentation to identify the client who owns such funds?
cases.answer_quote: Regulation 2.(8) requires a firm when it receives funds where it is not clear which client owns such funds or there is insufficient documentation to identify the client who owns such funds, within two business days, to either identify the client concerned or return the funds.

cases.question: How often does an investment firm have to check that the money it's holding for customers adds up to what it owes them?
cases.answer_quote: Each business day a firm should ensure that the aggregate balance on its client asset bank accounts (client money resource) as at the close of business on the previous business day is equal to the amount it should be holding on behalf of its clients (its client money requirement).

cases.question: How is the levy payable by each credit union capped?
cases.answer_quote: Since 2004 the amount of the levy payable by each credit union has been capped at a rate of .01% of its total assets as at September the previous year.

cases.question: Do insurers that only cover risks for their own corporate parent get lighter treatment when preparing for a financial crisis?
cases.answer_quote: Pre-emptive recovery planning is relevant to a captive insurer however, given that its principle relationship is to the group of which it is a part of, a more simplified strategic analysis is likely to be appropriate.

cases.question: Does the provision of exempt services by credit unions require an approval from the Central Bank?
cases.answer_quote: The provision of exempt services by credit unions does not require an approval (for additional services) from the Central Bank under the 1997 Act but provision of the service is subject to compliance with the relevant conditions, as set out in the Exempt Services Schedule.

cases.question: When the regulator vets someone for a senior role, does it look at whether they'll actually have enough hours to do the job?
cases.answer_quote: All F&P assessments must include an assessment of the amount of time that an applicant is proposing to give, or can give, to fully discharge the responsibilities of the role.

cases.question: What do chatbots allow consumers to do when engaging with their financial service provider?
cases.answer_quote: Automated bots or “chatbots” allow consumers to engage with their financial service provider via text message, instant messaging or voice activation services in natural-style conversations

cases.question: How can DLT collapse the two-step model of trading and settlement?
cases.answer_quote: It can collapse the two-step model of trading and settlement into a single process by embedding transaction records directly into a shared ledger and remove or reduce the need for various reconciliations in payments.

cases.question: What happens if a firm is slow paying its annual bill for being regulated?
cases.answer_quote: Prompt payment will be encouraged by the imposition of additional charges where levies are paid more than 35 (or more than 65 days) after the due date.

cases.question: Within how many business days must a regulated entity issue a premium rebate to a consumer?
cases.answer_quote: A regulated entity must issue a premium rebate to a consumer within five business days of the rebate becoming due.

cases.question: Can my bank ring me out of the blue to sell me something just because I'm already a customer?
cases.answer_quote: A regulated entity must not, for sales or marketing purposes, make an unsolicited personal visit or telephone call, at any time, to a personal consumer who is an existing consumer unless that personal consumer has given informed consent in writing to being contacted by the regulated entity by means of a personal visit or telephone call.
